title: Error Taxonomy: Retry, Repair, Escalate
objective: After this lesson you will be able to classify tool/model errors (transient, auth, invalid, downstream-down, budget-exhausted), assign retry/repair/escalate policies per class with budgets, and ban blind retry by checklist.
why: Uniform error handling fails uniformly: blind retries burn quotas on auth errors, silent catches hide invalid args, crashes on transients abandon recoverable work. Classified errors route correctly — transients backoff, auth escalates, invalid repairs once then quarantines, downstreams cascade to fallbacks. Taxonomy converts error handling from catch-all hope into per-class policy.

blocks.text: **Transient** (timeouts, rate limits, 5xx): backoff with jitter + attempt/time budgets, then escalate. **Auth** (401/403, expired keys): zero retries — escalate + rotate immediately (retrying burns + logs secrets). **Invalid** (schema violations, bad args): repair once with quoted error, then quarantine. **Downstream-down** (dependency outage): fallback cascade (Ch.4 Production). **Budget-exhausted** (caps hit): escalate with trail, never extend silently.

blocks.caption: Classes route to policies; policies carry budgets; budgets escalate

blocks.text: Invalid-argument failures get **one repair attempt** with the violation quoted back (schema error text included), then quarantine with evidence. Unbounded repair loops hallucinate fixes onto broken premises; single repair respects the model's fix rate while bounding the burn. Quarantine preserves raw inputs for parser tuning — the OpenDataLoader discipline, applied to tool calls.

Retries need **jitter** (randomized backoff spreads thundering herds) and **idempotency** (repeated side effects dedupe by key — Production Ch.7/Ch.4 patterns). Retry storms (synchronized clients hammering recovery) have caused more outages than the original faults — jittered, budgeted, keyed retries are the only safe kind.

blocks.title: Classify and route
blocks.note: Run it: expect 6/6 classifications plus the auth policy lookup (escalate-noretry). Unknown codes fall to budget/escalate — safe default for unrecognized failures, never blind retry.

items: Five classes (transient/auth/invalid/downstream/budget) with retry/repair/escalate policies + budgets
Repair once with quoted errors, then quarantine; jitter + idempotency guard all retries
Unknown errors default to escalate — safe fallback for unrecognized failures

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice classifier on all six cases and map classes. (b) Add RATE_LIMIT handling proof (classify + state its backoff policy from POLICIES). (c) Write the blind-retry ban as a code-review checklist line with the exception that proves the rule.
hints: Baseline 6/6: 503/RATE_LIMIT/TIMEOUT transient; 401/403 auth; 400/SCHEMA invalid; DOWN downstream; unknown budget.
RATE_LIMIT → transient: backoff [200,800,2000] + jitter, then escalate (never hammer recovery).
Checklist: 'Every retry names its class + budget; blanket catch-retry requires written justification' — the exception proves enforcement.
exercise.why: Classification coverage (all six incl. unknown), policy proof (backoff stages), and process enforcement (checklist line) are the three error-handling judgments — each verified, with blind retry banned structurally.
exercise.code: // Error-policy pattern: classify → budgeted policy → escalate with evidence.

quiz.q: 401 on a tool call, retried 5x with backoff. Verdict?
options: Harmful: auth errors never retry — escalate + rotate immediately; retries burn quota and log secrets
quiz.explain: Auth failures are credential problems, not transient ones. Retrying authenticates nothing and exposes secrets repeatedly.

quiz.q: Unknown error code from a new dependency. Default policy?
options: Escalate with trail (budget class): unrecognized failures route safe, never retried blindly
quiz.explain: Unknowns default to escalate-with-evidence: the safe fallback for failures outside the taxonomy. Taxonomies grow by classifying unknowns post-incident.

quiz.q: Synchronized clients hammer a recovering service. Missing?
options: Jitter on backoff: synchronized retries become retry storms worse than original faults
quiz.explain: Identical backoffs synchronize into storms. Jitter spreads load; idempotency dedupes effects. Both required for safe retries.

summary: Classify first (five classes), policy per class with budgets, repair once quoted, jitter + idempotency on retries, unknowns escalate. Blind retry banned by checklist.
next: Failures routed — now visibility: traces, replay, dry runs, and time-travel that make bugs reproducible. Next: debugging infrastructure.
